name: Spire Atelier Seasonal Couture Shell
description:
A structured outer garment from one of the Spire's exclusive fashion ateliers, designed to be worn for exactly one social season before being replaced. The Shell is constructed from materials that intentionally degrade after 90 days — the fabric loses its sheen, the structure collapses, the color fades. It is designed to be beautiful, temporary, and disposable.

The Seasonal Shell embodies the Spire's relationship with consumption — wealth expressed through the ability to discard. Wearing last season's Shell is a social disaster; wearing a Shell that hasn't begun to degrade proves you just bought it. The garment is a countdown timer worn as fashion.
functionality: Seasonal fashion display, social currency, planned obsolescence
what_it_says: You can afford to wear something designed to destroy itself, and you'll buy another when it does.
story_hooks: A Seasonal Shell that should have degraded months ago is still pristine — its owner either found a way to preserve it or it was manufactured outside the atelier system by someone who understood the materials but rejected the philosophy.
related_entities: ARCTURUS DEFENSE Bastion Subdermal Armor Mesh

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, architectural outer layer that commands presence through geometric precision. Sharp shoulders, clean lines, and an almost sculptural silhouette that reads as aggressive luxury. On the wearer, it creates an impression of controlled perfection — a walking statement of exclusive access and disposable wealth.
physical_description.fit: Tailored close to the body with structured panels that maintain their shape through advanced synthetic boning. The fit is intentionally rigid, almost uncomfortable, designed to showcase the garment's newness and integrity.
physical_description.primary_material: Iridescent bio-composite synth-silk blended with crystalline polymer threads that catch light across the visible spectrum. The base weave is a proprietary Spire material engineered to break down on a precise molecular schedule.
physical_description.texture: Initially glossy and almost liquid-smooth, with a subtle ripple across the surface from the crystalline weave. As degradation progresses, the texture becomes dull and papery, eventually fragmenting into a soft, lint-like surface.
physical_description.color_scheme: Shifts between jewel tones depending on light angle — deep violet transitioning to electric teal, with hints of rose gold at the seams. Within 60 days, these colors flatten and desaturate into muted, washed-out versions of themselves.
physical_description.closures: Invisible magnetic micro-clasps along the front placket, seamless and flush. They function perfectly for exactly 90 days before the embedded ferrite degrades.
distinctive_features: Spire House insignia embroidered in platinum thread at the collarbone — this fades to gray within 45 days
Dated QR code embedded in the inner seam tracking the exact manufacturing timestamp
Structural panels that maintain shape through phase-locked polymer that becomes limp and drooping as the chemical bonds break
Intentional micro-perforations that become visible holes as the material degrades
A barely-perceptible shimmer that dulls to matte within weeks
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 1 apex luxury — the garment costs 8,500 Φ and is explicitly designed to be unwearable after 90 days. Only the highest corpo elite can afford this calculated waste.
physical_description.cultural_context: Spire denizen, ultra-wealthy corpo class with access to exclusive seasonal ateliers. Wearing a fresh Shell signals you just spent serious capital on something you will discard. Wearing a degrading Shell shows you purchased it 'this season.' Wearing last season's Shell is social death. This is consumption as conspicuous performance art.
physical_description.condition_typical: New garments are pristine and stunning, with perfect shimmer and saturation. Mid-season (45 days), visible dulling begins. Late-season (75+ days), the structure visibly collapses, colors fade dramatically, and the wearer looks slightly disheveled despite the garment's intentions. Post-90 days: unwearable, destined for 'Spire Archive' museums or black-market Tier 5 resellers.
